methods.label: Find the favorable starting times
methods.explanation:
Assume that Leah's starting time is uniformly distributed within one complete cycle. The cycle lasts \(30+3+30=63\) seconds, so probability can be found by dividing the length of the favorable starting times by \(63\).

Let \(t\), with \(0\le t<63\), be the number of seconds after green begins. The next transitions occur at times \(30\), \(33\), and \(63\). To see a transition during the next three seconds, Leah must start within the three seconds immediately preceding one of these times. Apart from endpoints, the favorable starting times are
\[
(27,30)\cup(30,33)\cup(60,63).
\]
These intervals have disjoint interiors and total length \(9\). Including or excluding their endpoints does not affect the probability, since any exact starting time has probability zero under the uniform model. Therefore,
\[
\Pr(\text{a color change})=\frac{9}{63}=\frac17.
\]
The distribution assumption matters. A starting phase chosen uniformly from \((0,1)\) always gives three seconds of green, so the probability is \(0\). A starting phase chosen uniformly from \((28,29)\) always crosses the transition at \(30\), so the probability is \(1\). Thus the wording alone does not specify a unique probability. Under the standard uniform-phase interpretation, the answer is \(\frac17\), choice D.
